newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns rating of A to Czech Export Bank bond.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns rating of A to Czech Export Bank bond.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it had assigned a long-term rating of A to the upcoming Eurodollar bond of the Czech Export Bank, the Czech government's export credit agency.
The rating was based on the Czech Republic's unconditional and irrevocable guarantee of the bond, and reflected the government's rating, the agency said in a statement.
The outlook is stable, it added.
Czech Export Bank, established in March 1995, is a 100 percent state-controlled government agency, S&P said.

"The Czech Republic's "A' foreign currency rating reflects the government's prudent economic management, comfortable external financial position and high degree of fiscal flexibility, resulting from the government's broadly balanced budgets and low gross debt burden of 16 percnet of DGP at year-year 1996."
